Brown Act
Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider.
The legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance
with the open meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless
it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The
governing body may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future meeting.

Report on Posting

correct copy of the foregoing Meeting Agenda was properly posted on September 3, 2026 at
5:30 p.m., as required by law.

Public Communications
Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be
addressed directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Parks & Recreation
Commissions Meeting will be summarized by the Parks Director, not read in its entirety. A
copy of the email will be provided to the Commissioners and will also be available at the City
Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for public record and
noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

   Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  May 14, 2026

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Commissioner Trujillo

ROLL CALL - by Noemi Aguilera, Secretary
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Ruiz, Secretary Cynthia Esquivel and Commissioner Eric Trujillo;
Commissioner Pelayo arrived late at 7:01 pm.
Staff: Acting Director of Parks & Recreation Tina De La Rosa, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, Aquatics
Supervisor Leslie Consuegra and Recreation Coordinator Franklin Arroyo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident – Disappointed with response from Council regarding Zoom
meetings. Expressed gratitude for Vice Chair Ruiz. Disappointed in the attempt to remove Commissioner
Trujillo.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. ORAL REPORT ON COMMISSION GOVERNANCE AND PROCEDURAL REQUIREMENTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Trujillo
Acting Director De La Rosa introduced City Attorney Raul Salinas, who reviewed this item. He went into
details on the Brown Act and Robert’s Rules or Order, and how the Commissioners should respond to
Agenda Item questions or questions from the public.

Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident – Questioned who the Brown Act applies to. Asked multiple
questions including referring to the item.

2. ANNUAL PARTER ORGANIZATION REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Trujillo
Acting Director De La Rosa noted that JAA representative had an emergency and had to excuse themselves.
She then introduced A.Y.S.O. representative Lorraine Cortez who reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.
Then Acting Director De La Rosa introduced SGAC representative Ginette Tavares as well as Aquatics
Supervisor Leslie Consuegra who reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.

Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident – Would like an item report included at the next meeting
showing cost analysis and a number on how much residents pay for these programs.

3. RECREATION 3RD QUARTER REVIEW & UPCOMING EVENTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Secretary Esquivel
Acting Director De La Rosa introduced Aquatics Supervisor Leslie Consuegra who reviewed the aquatics
portion of this item; a discussion ensued. Acting Director De La Rosa then introduced Recreation

Parks & Recreation Commission Minutes of May 14, 2026  Page 1 of 3
  4
 Coordinator Franklin Arroyo who reviewed the rest of this item. Commissioners expressed gratitude for the
various events and the great job by staff. Commissioner Trujillo asked about Teen Center services, a
conversation ensued. Secretary Esquivel complimented the Easter Fest baby soft area and was thankful for
having a great Opening Day for the JAA.

4. GROUNDS & FACILITIES MAINTENANCE 3RD QUARTER REVIEW
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Trujillo
Parks Superintendent Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued by Commissioner Pelayo and Vice
Chair Ruiz regarding the cleaning of park restrooms. Acting Director De La Rosa confirmed that restrooms
will be cleaned at least twice a day through FY 26/27 as requested by Council. Secretary Esquivel expressed
concern for potholes in park parking lots to which Acting Director De La Rosa advised will report to Public
Works and wait for them to respond.

Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident - Stated he would like the city to plant specific flowers at more
parks. Stated that CDBG funds could have been used to provide wi-fi at the GCH and for other minor fixes
around the park. Recommended that park lights can be added by looking into using funding that Metro
provides, that other cities like Downey use.

5. PROPOSED PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSIONS MEETING SCHEDULED FY 2026/27
Recommended Motion: Approve proposed meetings with any suggested changes for the upcoming fiscal
year.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Trujillo
Acting Director De La Rosa reviewed this item; a discussion ensued between the Commissioners.

Recognized:

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Acting Director De La Rosa: Gardendale Tot Lot resurfacing Project will open next week. The Sports Center
Gymnasium scoreboard has been installed, just pending to install the shot clock reset which can currently
only be done manually. Street Soccer USA opened at Hollydale Regional Park with two pitches available to
play. The Swim Stadium scoreboard should be installed soon, waiting on delivery of equipment at the end
of May or early June with completion expected by the end of June. Currently gathering information from
two companies for the RFP for the LED lighting renovations for the baseball diamonds. A walkthrough was
conducted for the shade structures for the baseball diamonds. Some of the baseball fields are inoperable
due to recent wire theft at the park and staff is working with teams to accommodate as baseball season
just started. On April 18, the Miss South Gate pageant, Special Olympics, basketball tournament and Dear
Soul, Alma Querida events took place. The spa at the pool will reopen on May 15. JAA Opening Day,
Marichi Fest and Aquatics Fitness Expo all took place on May 2. The Spring Fit 5k was held on May 2 with
over 1,200 registered with 800 participating in the rec part and about 350 competitive runners. An 80’s
Bootcamp was held at the Sports Center that was a lot of fun, participants dressed in 80’s gear. The Teen
Center has added some hourly staff and has helped with fun events like an escape room and laser tag. The
teens really enjoy these events put together for them. Eco Garden class is being held on June 6, Zine
Festival on June 27 encouraged all to attend. Water Safety Bash is on May 16, Spring Golf Tournament on
May 17, Summer Kickoff on June 3 and Street Soccer USA will be hosting a World Cup viewing party on
June 12. Mayor Barron, Chamber of Commerce, along with AYSO are developing a food passport to get
discounts at local businesses.

Parks & Recreation Commission Minutes of May 14, 2026  Page 2 of 3
  5
 A survey for future use was discussed for the community to suggest changes or programs they would like in
the future.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Commissioner Trujillo: Mentioned that the gate at Hollydale Regional Park was locked, was curious of the
reasoning.

Vice Chair Ruiz: Attended the Swim Stadium open house and the 5K, happy with these events.

Secretary Esquivel: Also attended 5K, thankful for staff handling all events well. JAA Opening Day was
great.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS - Commissioner Trujillo asked for report on Wi-Fi setup and
cost for the Girls Clubhouse, possible funding from donations for this. Commissioner Pelayo would like
further discussion for the gate at Hollydale Regional Park to accommodate parents. Also, a report on what
the requirements are for partner organizations to use City facilities and what the cost is to the City.

ADJOURNMENT - At 9:52 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Vice Chair Ruiz

Respectfully submitted:

Cynthia Esquivel, Secretary

Subject:  Annual  Review  of Fee Waivers  FY 2025/26

Recommended  Motion:  Motion  to receive  & file and forward  the attached  report to the
City Council

ReportSummaiy:  The department's  Fee Waiver  policy requires  that staff report
quarterly to the Commission  on all fee waivers that are approved as well as providing an
annual summary  report that will be forwarded  to the City Council.  The purpose of this
report is to ensure that staff is implementing  and interpreting  the policy as intended, to
provide feedback or clarify policy if needed and to allow the Commission  and Council to
monitor the impacts that these uses and the associated  fees that are waived have on
the overall budget and operation of the department.

Attached  is a complete  listing of the fee waivers that were approved  during the past
fiscal year.  Please be aware that this list does not include non-fee use of city facilities
by partner organizations  such as the Junior Athletic Association  or the Aquatics  Swim
Club as these uses are now covered  under a separate  policy.  As requested  by the
Commission,  staff has also included a summary of all facility use permits issued and the
fees that were collected this past year for comparison.

The intent of our Park facilities  is to benefit the community  through  the offering  of
programs  and significant  and beneficial events.  The accommodation  of paid, private
events is a secondary  function and should not interfere with the primary purpose.  On
this basis, staff believes that the figures provided show a healthy and appropriate  use of
our facilities and believes that the fee waivers being provided are within the intent of the
policy provided.
